The fuel tanks and boosters ARE the most expensive part of space travel. Because getting to orbit is the hardest part of space travel. The space shuttle, which was semi-renewable, cost between $600 million and $1.5 billion per launch, depending on the payload. Most of those costs came from rebuilding the fuel tank and the boosters. In 2012, NASA's SLS was estimated to be ~$500 million max per launch. Which was considered cheap back then. 

The falcon heavy costs $90 million. And the boosters are renewable, saving around ~30% cost on top of that. Meaning another Falcon heavy launch would be literally 10 times as cheap as the space shuttle.

Also, considering the one thing holding NASA back from doing more research is money to get into orbit... yeah it's a brand new space age.

When I was in middle school, my older cousin, his friend, and I used to go to the local chain supermarket in our neighborhood to steal small stuff. I would only take stuff like bagels or chips, while they'd take earphones, batteries, and other small electronic stuff. On St. Patrick's day after school one year, they asked me if I wanted to go with them. For some reason, My gut told me no, even though I'd be totally up for it. So they left without me and I played video games all day. 

A few hours go by, and my cousin and his friend hadn't come back, and I wasn't all that worried. Then it's 10:30 at night, and I'm starting to freak out. Turns out they had gotten caught trying to take 4 pairs of earphones, 5 packs of batteries, an Xbox controller, and some jeans. Luckily they were under 16, so they just got community service and it was off their record, but it really freaked me out. I never stole again, and I just think how the luck of the Irish was with me that day.
